raw.details:
Bharat Academix Hackverse 2026

Build. Innovate. Solve.

Bharat Academix presents HACKVERSE 2026, an online technology hackathon where students, developers, researchers, and innovators come together to solve a real-world problem through technology.

The official problem statement will be released by the Bharat Academix team on Unstop on 14 October 2026. Participants will analyze the challenge, propose a solution, build a working prototype, and present their project to the jury.

Hackathon Format:

Round 1 — Idea & Solution Submission:

Date: 14–15 October 2026
Platform: Unstop

The official problem statement will be released on Unstop on 14 October. Participants must understand the challenge and submit their proposed solution through Unstop.

Submission should include:

  • Problem Understanding
  • Proposed Solution
  • Key Features
  • Technology Stack
  • Expected Impact
  • Implementation Approach

Selected teams will proceed to Round 2.

Round 2 — Build & Develop:

Date: 17–20 October 2026
Platform: Unstop

Shortlisted teams will develop their solution based on the official problem statement and submit their project through Unstop.

Required submission may include:

  • Working Prototype
  • GitHub Repository
  • Project Documentation
  • Demo Video
  • Deployment Link, if applicable

Round 3 — Final Demo & Jury:

Date: 25 October 2026
Platform: Online — Bharat Academix Team

Shortlisted finalists will present their projects online before the jury.

5 Minutes: Project Presentation & Live Demo
3 Minutes: Jury Q&A

Finalists will receive the online meeting details through their registered email/official communication channels.

Themes:

The problem statement may involve areas such as:

  • Artificial Intelligence & Generative AI
  • Machine Learning & Deep Learning
  • Computer Vision
  • Data Science & Analytics
  • Web & Mobile Development
  • Cybersecurity
  • EdTech
  • HealthTech
  • AgriTech
  • FinTech
  • Sustainability
  • Automation
  • Emerging Technologies

The exact problem statement and requirements will be announced on Unstop.

Team Size:

1–6 Members

Participants can participate individually or form a team of up to six members.

Who Can Participate?:

The hackathon is open to:

  • College and University Students
  • Engineering and Computer Science Students
  • MBA and Management Students
  • Developers
  • Researchers
  • AI/ML Enthusiasts
  • Data Scientists
  • Designers
  • Startup and Technology Enthusiasts

Technology:

There is no mandatory technology stack unless specified in the problem statement. Participants may use technologies such as Python, Java, C++, React, Next.js, Node.js, Flutter, TensorFlow, PyTorch, OpenCV, Generative AI, LLMs, RAG, APIs, databases, cloud platforms, and open-source technologies.

Judging Criteria:

Criteria Weightage
Technical Implementation 25%
Innovation & Creativity 20%
Working Prototype 20%
Problem Relevance & Impact 15%
UI/UX 10%
Scalability & Future Potential 10%
Total 100%

Awards & Recognition:

Awards may include:

  • Winner
  • First Runner-Up
  • Second Runner-Up
  • Best AI Solution
  • Most Innovative Solution
  • Best Technical Implementation
  • Best UI/UX
  • Best Startup Potential
  • Best Social Impact Solution

Eligible participants may also receive certificates based on their participation and performance.

Important Dates:

Stage Date Platform
Problem Statement Release 14 October 2026 Unstop
Round 1 — Idea Submission 14–15 October 2026 Unstop
Round 2 — Build & Develop 17–18 October 2026 Unstop
Round 3 — Final Demo & Jury 20 October 2026 Online — Bharat Academix

Important Guidelines:

  • The official problem statement will be released on Unstop on 14 October 2026.
  • Round 1 and Round 2 submissions must be completed through Unstop.
  • Participants must submit their work within the specified deadlines.
  • Plagiarism or unauthorized copying may result in disqualification.
  • Participants must have appropriate rights to use all code, datasets, APIs, models, and other project components.
  • Participants must be able to explain and demonstrate their project.
  • GitHub and demo links must be accessible to the evaluation team.
  • Participants must follow the official hackathon guidelines and submission requirements.

Why Participate?:

HACKVERSE 2026 gives participants an opportunity to solve a real-world challenge, build a working technology solution, strengthen their skills, showcase their innovation, build their portfolio, and gain practical hackathon experience.

The problem will be revealed on 14 October.

You bring the skills.
We bring the challenge.
You build the solution.

Bharat Academix Hackverse 2026

Build. Innovate. Solve.
